title: The Material Editor 🧪
description: Navigate the node‑based graph where materials come to life.

slides.title: Meet the Editor 🖥️
slides.content:
# The Material Lab

When you open a Material asset, you enter a specialised editor with these key areas:

* **Viewport** – real‑time preview of the material on a mesh.
* **Graph** – the canvas where you connect **Material Expression** nodes.
* **Palette** (right side) – list of all available expression nodes, categorised.
* **Details Panel** – properties of the selected node.
* **Stats Panel** – shows number of shader instructions (performance indicator).

*Analogy:* It's like a **chemistry set** – you mix ingredients (nodes) and observe the result in the viewport.

quizData.question: The Material Editor uses the same node graph system as Blueprints.
quizData.explanation: Both use node‑based editing, but Material nodes handle colour and math, not execution flow.

slides.title: The Main Material Node 🎯
slides.content:
# The Heart of It All

Every Material graph has one **Main Material Node** (the big one in the center). It has a series of input pins that define the final surface:

* **Base Color** – colour or texture
* **Metallic** – 0 or 1 (or texture)
* **Specular** – specular intensity (default 0.5)
* **Roughness** – smoothness
* **Emissive Color** – glow effect
* **Opacity** – transparency (requires Blend Mode change)
* **Normal** – detail bump map
* **World Position Offset** – vertex animation

You connect expressions to these pins to build the material.

slides.title: Inputs & Outputs Colour Coding 🌈
slides.content:
## Reading the Wires

Unlike Blueprint execution wires, all Material wires are **data wires** (colours):

* **Grey** – scalar (float)
* **Red/Green/Blue** – vector (3 floats)
* **White** – any type

You'll mainly use grey (numbers) and RGB (colours). Connecting incompatible types shows an error.

quizData.question: Which Main Material Node input makes a surface glow?
quizData.explanation: Emissive Color adds self‑illumination, making the surface appear to glow even in shadow.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use the Palette

Drag nodes from the **Palette** instead of right‑clicking. It's categorised and faster once you know the node names. Enable it via **Window → Palette** if hidden.
